levels.must: Fix on sight: leading journals almost never print this, or it is internal material.
levels.review: Judge in context: often a tell, sometimes the right word.
levels.density: Normal in leading journals; reported only as a rate per 1000 words.

designs.observational: Cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies, including analyses of routine and public databases
designs.systematic-review: Systematic reviews, meta-analyses and scoping reviews
designs.diagnostic: Diagnostic accuracy and test evaluation studies
designs.modelling: Disease, transmission and burden models, projections and forecasts
designs.laboratory: Laboratory and mechanistic studies (cell, animal, structural, device)
designs.computational: Bioinformatics, genomics and other computational studies
designs.prediction: Clinical prediction models, development and validation
designs.mendelian-randomisation: Mendelian randomisation and other genetic-epidemiology designs

families.lancet: The Lancet and its specialty journals
families.nature: Nature and the Nature research journals

scopes.caption: Figure legends and table titles or notes
scopes.figure: Text inside figures, read from plotting code or SVG

categories.CON: Contrast frames used as a rhetorical device
categories.DEF: Defensive hedging, disclaimers and pre-emptive rebuttals
categories.META: Process or metadata narration that is not about the research
categories.ENG: Engineering or software register used for research procedures
categories.LEX: Vocabulary that leading journals rarely print
categories.HYG: Internal material that must not reach a publication
categories.PLAN: Research plans that are undecided or carry history
categories.LOG: Execution logs that will not read clearly later
categories.CODE: Analysis code and comments that block a rerun or a reader
